cases.name: boot time (POST -> every VM running)

invariants.name: every one of the 20 1-VM boots came up (no VM failed)
every one of the 20 8-VM boots came up (no VM failed)
every one of the 10 50-VM boots came up (no VM failed)

notes: 1-VM boot: n=20 p50=21ms p95=39ms p99=43ms max=43ms
8-VM boot: n=20 p50=219ms p95=257ms p99=283ms max=283ms

the sweep boots a long-lived guest (beats unset) so 'every VM came up running' is a stable contract; a self-rebooting guest can have already finished its beats when the POST reply is read, which is churn rather than a boot failure, and the console line that would tell the two apart races the guest reset it precedes
no boot-time threshold is configured in this repository (no in-repo boot budget exists), so these are measurements; pass --boot-p95-ms to enforce a bar

cases.vector: 50 x 1 vCPU x 128 MiB fleet with a 16 MiB workspace volume per VM

invariants.name: the fleet holds one workspace copy per VM (50 x 16 MiB of image)
whole-fleet RSS under the 8 GiB budget with a workspace volume

notes: 50-VM --workspace boot (POST -> running): 3087ms
fleet 50 with workspace: RSS baseline 4 MiB peak 5894 MiB; CPU [2.5, 2.5, 2.25]% of one core

the 800 MiB of copies are host memory, not guest RSS: this host's harness work directory is under /tmp (tmpfs), so their pages are charged to Shmem — which went 4973 -> 5773 MiB (0 MiB off the copies' 800 MiB) while the fleet ran. Host-wide Cached (42339 -> 43326 MiB) moved for the whole host's reasons and is not attributed to the fleet. noded's RSS is what the 8 GiB criterion measures and does not carry the copies, so a fleet's true host cost is that RSS plus them — recorded here so it is not understated

steady-state CPU with the volume attached is 2.500% of one core versus 2.499547079566145% without it in this run: the guest's ext4 journal adds no measurable steady-state cost here (the case without a workspace carries the 0.03%-baseline finding)

image.provenance: built by scripts/mk-workspace-image.sh: a 16 MiB ext4 with a pinned label, UUID and superblock time. Identity is stable across builds; the bytes are not reproducible (mke2fs randomises the journal UUID and this e2fsprogs has no -J uuid=), which is the block slice's own note

budget regression check: comparing against acceptance-server-budgets-2026-10-11.json

findings.title: steady-state CPU does not reproduce the recorded 0.03% baseline
findings.detail: measured peak 2.500% of one core for 50 guests with the fleet's own beats configuration versus the 0.03% recorded in PORT_STATUS slice 16. The configured bar (5.0%) still passes, with a thin margin. At n=2 the same configuration measures 0.250%. The recorded figure was sampled with the guests 'parked in HLT', which measures no heartbeat writes and no console polling; noded never boots a parked guest (its cmdline builder has no halt option), and every guest it does boot writes a heartbeat every 5 s and polls its console every second, plus the run watcher's 5 ms poll pass. Those wakeups are the measured cost. A like-for-like baseline is needed: either re-sample the recorded figure with the same guest configuration, or expose a parked-guest option through noded so both states can be measured.

findings.title: a restarted daemon reuses run-r1 and overwrites the previous instance's workspace copy
findings.detail: noded's run ids restart with the daemon (`Registry::new` sets `next_seq = 0`), so the first run after a restart is `r1` again and its workspace directory is /tmp/apz-acceptance-server-h2c791o5/budgets-workspace-restore-a-uds/run-r1 — the very directory the killed daemon's run r1 was using. `materialize_workspaces` copies the base image onto that path with `std::fs::copy`, which truncates the existing copy in place, so the previous instance's retained volume (sha256 af48b69adb1750c408bfdc824cac5bbf6c1a6d1afd1f688357ada34c9777d286) is replaced (sha256 a6d7281595cd60234f1f2f028790f6f23a4e7264309037c4a28ac395f89b6031) and its /workspace/notes.txt marker is gone. The block slice's contract that a run's copies stay after the run (they hold the agent's work) therefore holds only within one daemon lifetime: restarting on the same --uds-dir destroys the retained volumes of the runs whose ids the new daemon re-issues. Both behaviours are deliberate on their own (run ids are per-daemon; copies are kept), which is the conflict this cell records.
findings.expected: the retained copy of a finished/killed run keeps its bytes across a daemon restart (or the new run is given a path that cannot collide with one)
findings.reproducer: noded --workspace IMG --uds-dir D; POST {n:1,beats:40}; console `wspace TOKEN`; `sync`; SIGTERM noded; noded --workspace IMG --uds-dir D; POST {n:1} -> the new run is r1 and D/run-r1/workspace-0.ext4 no longer contains TOKEN
findings.suspected_component: crates/noded/src/registry.rs (reserve_run_id / boot_run run-dir path) + crates/vmm/src/spawner.rs (materialize_workspaces copies in place)

findings.title: no egress allowlist exists to test
findings.detail: the persona's egress-denial surface assumes an egress proxy (decision 0010 names one for a later milestone). In this MVP the only wire is the per-VM UDS muxer, so the suite asserts the structural equivalent (only the created listeners exist, no AF_VSOCK, no NIC) instead of a denial that cannot occur
